items.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021
items.q: I was in the saxophone section with Miguel Zenon, the great alto player.

ctx.x: Did the hang translate, help translate into your stage presence, which I observe as welcoming and an addition to what you can present?

You know it’s interesting, I mean first of all I’m glad you feel it’s welcoming and you know I don’t know if it’s the hang — I think part of what made me feel comfortable on stage was being part of an Afro-Cuban band — it’s a band in Boston called, it used to be called Mango Blue, then it became Mango Blues, and I was in the saxophone section with Miguel Zenon, the great alto player. And I didn’t know much about Afro-Cuban music or all the South American rhythm, it was all new to me, but another thing that was…
moving to the moment and being in the moment I don’t think about the stage as a stage. I just think it’s like let’s just all celebrate the moment.
